A Point of View: Why we should defend the right to be offensive

I am fine with defending the right of speakers to be "offensive," whatever that exactly means. I am also okay with defending the rights of people to lie, as we can never trust a truth police.

The problem arises where free speech is used as a cloak for precisely the opposite -- censorship.

Where a consolidated media with strong pecuniary interests in wars pushes a distorted narrative that all the people of a certain religion, or ethnicity, or nationality, or whatever the identity characteristic is, other views are naturally left out of the equation.

While this situation can never be fully fixed, there are neutral ways to reduce the imbalance and "crowding out" of free speech.

  1. Break up the media. A media with more owners will provide more different free speech views.

  2. Remove the extra free speech rights given to large pieces of property and maintain free speech for living people.

  3. Be aware that, as is the case here, when large corporate entities pursue a narrative that conveniently aligns with their war interests, that the full story is not being provided. Ideally, we should actively campaign against such a narrative. For some, campaigning, arguing, disagreeing is uncomfortable, so at least don't promote these things.

Touching the media is delicate thing, perhaps too difficult for the average government: Abuse is easy and hard to revert.

And please, make no mistake, I do believe that media should never be allowed to become an effective tool of propaganda / censorship. I personally believe that your point 1 is undeniably necessary... and difficult to fuck up.
